reason: The narrative contains multiple regular people characters who exercise significant agency throughout the text. The people of Shechem collectively make decisions—they listen to Abimelech, hire Gaal, later conspire against Abimelech, and set ambushes. Gaal son of Ebed is an ordinary figure who gains the people's trust, opposes Abimelech, and takes military action. Zebul exercises authority as a city official. Most notably, an unnamed woman takes decisive action by throwing a millstone that kills Abimelech, and a young armor-bearer makes the choice to strike the fatal blow. Even ordinary laborers harvest grapes and celebrate. The narrative is substantially driven by the choices and actions of these regular people rather than being controlled solely by elite figures.
